viking1.name: Viking 1 Lander
viking1.realLocation: Chryse Planitia ("Plains of Gold"), northern Mars
viking1.purpose: Take the first pictures from the surface of Mars and test the soil and air for signs of life.
viking1.howItWorked: A robotic arm scooped soil into tiny onboard labs. They heated it, fed it nutrients, and sniffed the gases that came out.
viking1.discovery: Mars soil reacted in surprising ways, but no living things or organic molecules were confirmed. Scientists still debate the results today.
viking1.whyStopped: It worked for more than 6 years. In November 1982 a wrong command sent from Earth cut off communication for good.
viking1.funFact: Viking 1 sent back the very first photo ever taken on the surface of Mars, a picture of its own foot!

evidenceCard.title: Active Soil
evidenceCard.clue: Mars soil is chemically active, but Viking could NOT prove there is life.

opportunity.name: Opportunity Rover
opportunity.realLocation: Meridiani Planum, near the Martian equator
opportunity.purpose: Act like a robot geologist: drive around and find rocks that remember if water was ever there.
opportunity.howItWorked: Solar panels powered six wheels, cameras, and a robotic arm with a rock grinder and microscope.
opportunity.discovery: It found tiny round "blueberries" made of hematite and layered rocks. Both usually form in water. Mars was once wet!
opportunity.whyStopped: A giant dust storm covered the whole planet in 2018 and blocked the sunlight its solar panels needed.
opportunity.funFact: It was planned to work for 90 Mars days but kept going for almost 15 years and drove farther than a marathon!

evidenceCard.title: Water Rocks
evidenceCard.clue: Some Mars rocks formed in water a very long time ago.

phoenix.name: Phoenix Mars Lander
phoenix.realLocation: Vastitas Borealis, the icy plains near the north pole
phoenix.purpose: Dig into the frozen ground near the north pole and study ice and soil.
phoenix.howItWorked: A robotic arm dug small trenches. Ovens on the lander heated soil samples to see what was inside.
phoenix.discovery: Bright white chunks in a trench disappeared after a few days. They were water ice turning straight into vapor. Phoenix also confirmed water in a heated soil sample.
phoenix.whyStopped: Polar winter arrived. Without enough sunlight its solar panels stopped working, and contact was lost in November 2008.
phoenix.funFact: The scientists nicknamed the trench where the ice vanished "Dodo-Goldilocks".

evidenceCard.title: Hidden Ice
evidenceCard.clue: There is frozen water ice on Mars today, just under the soil.
